title: C. The Number Of Good Substrings

legend: You are given a binary string s%%ZSMJ0%% (recall that a string is binary if each character is either 0%%ZSMJ1%% or 1%%ZSMJ2%%).

Let f(t)%%ZSMJ3%% be the decimal representation of integer t%%ZSMJ4%% written in binary form (possibly with leading zeroes). For example f(011)=3,f(00101)=5,f(00001)=1,f(10)=2,f(000)=0%%ZSMJ5%% and f(000100)=4%%ZSMJ6%%.
The substring sl,sl+1,…,sr%%ZSMJ7%% is good if r−l+1=f(sl…sr)%%ZSMJ8%%.
For example string s=1011%%ZSMJ9%% has 5%%ZSMJ10%% good substrings: s1…s1=1%%ZSMJ11%%, s3…s3=1%%ZSMJ12%%, s4…s4=1%%ZSMJ13%%, s1…s2=10%%ZSMJ14%% and s2…s4=011%%ZSMJ15%%.
Your task is to calculate the number of good substrings of string s%%ZSMJ16%%.
You have to answer t%%ZSMJ17%% independent queries.
input: The first line contains one integer t%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤t≤1000%%ZSMJ19%%) — the number of queries.
The only line of each query contains string s%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤|s|≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ21%%), consisting of only digits 0%%ZSMJ22%% and 1%%ZSMJ23%%.
output: For each query print one integer — the number of good substrings of string s%%ZSMJ25%%.
